subject.title: Deny same-provider cross-context message sends by default

question: Should OpenClaw intentionally change the shipped same-provider message-tool default from permissive to fail-closed, accepting that existing forwarding workflows must add an explicit opt-in?
rationale: The implementation can enforce either policy correctly, but source inspection cannot decide whether the security benefit outweighs the upgrade break for existing same-provider bridge and automation workflows.

options.title: Accept fail-closed default
options.body: Merge after exact-head live proof, retaining allowWithinProvider=true and the legacy override as documented compatibility paths.

options.title: Stage the default change
options.body: Keep the current default temporarily, add prominent migration diagnostics or deprecation guidance, and flip the default in a later planned release.

options.title: Keep permissive default
options.body: Retain opt-out behavior and treat current-conversation-only enforcement as an explicit operator policy rather than a global default.

recommendation.title: Accept fail-closed default
recommendation.body: Merge after exact-head live proof, retaining allowWithinProvider=true and the legacy override as documented compatibility paths.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent history spans the shared outbound, Telegram, and security-sensitive runtime surfaces involved in this rollout decision.
